newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bear Stearns trims Mexico inflation, peso forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Bear Stearns trims Mexico inflation, peso forecasts.

text.p: Brokerage Bear, Stearns & Co said Monday it cut its 1997 inflation and exchange rate forecasts for Mexico.

"Based on the strength of the peso and then increase in consumer prices so far this year, we are lowing our inflation forecase for 1997 to 14 from 15 percent," analysts David Malpass and Elizabeth Olson said in a daily report.
The analysts also said the brokerage marginally trimmed its average annual exchange rate forecast to 8.0 pesos to the dollar from 8.1.

Its forecast for economic growth remained unchanged at 5.6 percent, however, it said second half growth in gross domestic product would be supported by lower interest rates that could ease to 17 percent. ((--Daniel Perez-Whitaker, Monterrey newsroom +528 345 7617))
